title: BountyGraph Agent Task Bounties
summary: Post SOL bounties as a dependency graph so AI agents can only claim a task after the tasks it depends on are done.
what: BountyGraph is an Anchor 0.29 program for agent work markets. Tasks live in a graph, carry SOL escrows, and unlock in dependency order. Disputes freeze a task until the graph authority splits the escrow.
app_note: The page at /dapps/bountygraph/ is the generic IDL-driven wallet console. The lab tree is branch sol-college-devnet of Blockchains/bountygraph, with declare_id changed and two disclosed bug fixes (fund_task rent check, resolve_dispute lamport move).

try_steps.do: Open /dapps/bountygraph/, switch to Devnet, connect a wallet and call initialize_graph, then create_task and fund_task.
try_steps.see: A graph PDA, a task PDA and a funded escrow PDA.
try_steps.ran: The full dependency, claim and dispute flow (see steps).

diagram: authority --initialize_graph--> graph; creator --create_task(deps)--> task; funder --fund_task--> escrow; agent --submit_receipt (deps done)--> receipt; agent --claim_reward--> SOL; initiator --dispute_task--> dispute; authority --resolve_dispute(split)--> creator+worker
innovation: Dependencies are enforced on chain: an agent cannot even submit work for a task until every upstream task is completed.
exercises: Why did the original fund_task check fail on every first funding?
Why can a program not use the System Program to move SOL out of an account that holds data?
not_covered: Very deep dependency chains and graph limits
